clue.text: Chilly Fellow runs a degree course

parts.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for runs
PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a well-known Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A cold-mannered academic fellow runs a university course.
explanation.walkthrough: PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, the Oxford degree taken by many British politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Frappé describes a drink served iced or chilled with shaved ice, so it means cold.

clue.text: Note about much wickedness in the fleet

indicators.note: the note goes round the other words, enclosing them

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
a lot means much
ill means evil or wickedness

explanation.surface: A naval squadron gets a reprimand about its sins.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a small fleet of ships or boats.

clue.text: Status of a fellow taking up Rugby Union?

definitions.text: Status of a fellow taking up Rugby Union?

parts.note: a mate is a fellow or companion

indicators.note: in a down clue taking up reads the abbreviation upwards

explanation.surface: Asks what standing a man who starts playing rugby union has.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking up' reverses RU to UR. Rugby union was strictly amateur until 1995, so the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur plays without pay, the official status of rugby union players for a century.

clue.text: He'd paid out, eg to firm

indicators.note: out means the letters of the preceding words are put into disorder

explanation.surface: A man who settled a bill, for example, to a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' rearranges HEDPAIDEG; 'firm' is an adjective here (stubborn), not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigheaded means obstinately stubborn, unshakeable in opinion.

clue.text: Smoked, they produce carbon and damage hooters

definitions.text: Smoked, they produce carbon and damage hooters

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

indicators.note: to damage the word hooters is to knock its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A health warning: cigars give off carbon and harm the nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooters' is slang for noses, which smoke harms, and 'damage' is the anagram signal. Read as a whole, the clue also describes the cigars themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheroots are cigars cut square at both ends, smoked and giving off carbon.

clue.text: Three stage take-off from runway

parts.note: an athlete's three-part leap after a run-up, not an aircraft leaving an airstrip

explanation.surface: An aeroplane leaves the airfield in three stages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runway' suggests an airport; it is the athletics run-up strip for the triple jump.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the old name for the triple jump, an athletic event of three bounds.

clue.text: More ready to fall" — last words on Virgin Queen

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is the final inscription on a gravestone
Elizabeth I was the Virgin Queen, and ER is a queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: A dying monarch's final words, quoted as she declines.
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina; 'on' places RIP before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit that is riper is closer to dropping from the tree.

clue.text: Agent for some air supplies

parts.note: a chemical agent that provides oxygen, a part of air, not a spy or a supplier

explanation.surface: A supplier of some air, like a salesman for a gas company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agent' suggests a person; it is a chemical agent, and the part of air supplied is oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxidant is a substance that gives up oxygen in chemical reactions.

clue.text: Desire dramatically moving in this way?

definitions.text: Desire dramatically moving in this way?

parts.words: Desire dramatically moving in this way?
parts.note: Tennessee Williams' play names a tram called Desire, and a tram runs along a town road

explanation.surface: Asks whether passion in a play travels like this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desire' is the tram in A Streetcar Named Desire; streetcars run on the road named in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetcar travels along a street, as the play title A Streetcar Named Desire suggests.

clue.text: Resigned to Act I being changed by this order

definitions.text: Resigned to Act I being changed by this order

indicators.note: says the letters of the preceding words are being altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor submits to a scene change made by the script's instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being changed' rearranges RESIGNED TO ACT I; and a script's instruction can change Act I, so the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage direction is an instruction in a script telling actors how to move or act.

clue.text: Could be operating as an extremely colourful butterfly

indicators.note: says the letters of the following word could be arranged as something else

explanation.surface: A surgeon at work is likened to a vivid butterfly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' turns OPERATING into the butterfly; 'extremely colourful' hints that the colour sits at the wing tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The orange-tip is a British butterfly whose males have bright orange patches at their wing ends.

clue.text: Coming before a superior officer

explanation.surface: Something that precedes a senior official.
explanation.definitionFit: Prior means earlier or preceding, and it is also the title of a monastery's head under an abbot.

clue.text: Cold fish, showing little on the surface

explanation.surface: An unemotional person who reveals little of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotionally frosty person is called an iceberg, and a floating ice mass shows only a fraction above water.

clue.text: Ample room for spectators in Chester racecourse

indicators.note: signals that the letters sit inside the words Chester racecourse

explanation.surface: Chester's racecourse offers plenty of space for the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Chester is an English city with a famous racecourse; the answer runs across its two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a wide stepped standing area at a sports ground, with room for many watchers.

clue.text: Enticed from Leeward, so sailors say

indicators.note: points to the nautical pronunciation of the preceding word, as a seaman says it

parts.note: leeward, the side away from the wind, is said by sailors as 'loo-ard'

explanation.surface: Someone tempted away from the sheltered side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Lured means tempted or drawn in with bait.

clue.text: Pluckily remove a Van-dyke?

parts.note: a Vandyke is a pointed beard, and taking it out by plucking means stripping hair, not acting bravely

explanation.surface: Bravely getting rid of a painting by Van Dyck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluckily' suggests courage but means by plucking; a Vandyke is the pointed beard seen in Van Dyck's portraits.
explanation.definitionFit: To depilate is to take off body hair, as by plucking out a beard.

clue.text: Third man to dilute the antacid

parts.note: Harry Lime is the title character of the film The Third Man
to water a drink is to dilute it

explanation.surface: A third person waters down the stomach remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third man' suggests a cricket fielder; it is Harry Lime of the film The Third Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Limewater, a calcium hydroxide solution, neutralises acid and was taken for indigestion.

clue.text: Forceful check surrounds tough guys

indicators.note: the checking word goes round the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
he-men are macho tough guys

explanation.surface: A strong restraint is placed around some hard men.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means passionate and intense in expression.

clue.text: Parallel bars American sportsmen play on

explanation.surface: Gymnastic equipment on which US athletes compete.
explanation.definitionFit: A gridiron is a grill of parallel metal bars, and the name for an American football field.

clue.text: Stand taken by Sergeant, we hear

annotationWithheld.why: Stand taken by Sergeant, we hear (7) for ROSTRUM: no sound-alike for a sergeant's word gives ROSTRUM convincingly ('roster 'em' is a guess), and no source confirms the parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Stand taken by Sergeant, we hear

clue.text: The Walrus and the Alphabet

explanation.surface: Sounds like a title in the style of Lewis Carroll's 'The Walrus and the Carpenter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Morse is an old word for the walrus, and Morse code is the dot-and-dash signalling alphabet.

clue.text: Say "Ar" house-doctor states — here's a lozenge

parts.note: the letter R is pronounced 'ar'
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
US stands for United States

explanation.surface: A doctor's speech about houses ends with a throat sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lozenge' suggests a cough sweet; here it is the diamond shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhombus is a diamond-shaped figure, which in geometry and heraldry is called a lozenge.

clue.text: Service engineer

parts.note: an engineer in an armed service, not a repairman who services boilers

explanation.surface: Someone who comes to repair appliances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service engineer' suggests a repairman; it is an engineer in the armed services.
explanation.definitionFit: Sappers are private soldiers of the Royal Engineers, the British Army's engineering corps.

clue.text: Harmful element of scenario, edited to have no love in it

indicators.note: the word scenario is reworked into a new order, once a letter has gone

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A scriptwriter strips the romance from a toxic part of the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To have no love in it' takes O out of SCENARIO, leaving SCENARI, which 'edited' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a poisonous chemical element.

clue.text: Yarn of two cities in digest form

parts.note: NY is the short form of New York
LON is a short form of London

explanation.surface: A tale of two cities in condensed form, like a Reader's Digest version of Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: A popular legend says nylon was named from New York and London.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre spun into thread.

clue.text: Judges' exhibit — mass murder weapon

explanation.surface: A piece of evidence in a court case over a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judges' is the Old Testament book, not a courtroom: there Samson kills a thousand men with the jawbone of an ass.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Judges tells how Samson slew a thousand Philistines with an ass's jaw, a biblical massacre weapon.

clue.text: Good fairy left in danger

parts.note: a peri is a benevolent fairy of Persian legend

explanation.surface: A kindly fairy abandoned in a threatening spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious danger or jeopardy.

clue.text: One mum upset — dummy cannot be changed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: upset means the word mum is knocked into a different order

parts.note: in bridge the dummy hand is laid on the table, and players call it the table

explanation.surface: A mother is upset that a baby's dummy is irreplaceable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns MUM into MMU. In bridge, the dummy's cards are exposed and declarer plays 'from the table'.
explanation.definitionFit: Immutable means fixed and unalterable.

clue.text: Meditative talking-bird swallowed by large pigeon

indicators.note: the bird word is taken inside the pigeon word, as if eaten

parts.note: the runt is a breed of very large domestic pigeon
mina is a spelling of mynah, the bird that mimics speech

explanation.surface: A thoughtful parrot-like bird is gulped down by a big pigeon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruminant animal chews the cud, and figuratively ruminant means given to pondering.

clue.text: No 2 to take chair bottoms up

parts.note: pro- as a prefix marks a deputy, as in pro-vice-chancellor, the number two
to take a chair is to sit

explanation.surface: A deputy is asked to sit down at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO here is the deputy prefix of pro-vice-chancellor or proconsul.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a Latin-derived drinking toast, like cheers.
